axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps the Cloudflare platform
(Workers, Pages, D1, R2, DNS, docs retrieval, etc.) as tools for agents.
axes.runtime:
Primarily an official hosted remote server (the docs carry a remote-endpoint line) + runnable locally; GitHub 4,431★,
last push 2026-10-22 (API verified).
axes.local_files: Reads and writes no local project files — the scope is Cloudflare account resources (deploying Workers, writing D1/R2, etc.).
axes.background: The remote form lives on Cloudflare's side; no background-task semantics (deploy actions complete immediately).
axes.tools:
Grouped by product (Workers/Pages/D1/R2/DNS/Docs…), trimmable via configuration; write capability is complete
(deploying Workers, creating KV/D1 databases, changing DNS records). The complete grouping follows the repo README.
axes.context: No cross-session memory — state lives in the Cloudflare account resources themselves.
axes.permissions:
**API-token permissions = agent permissions**: Cloudflare tokens can narrowly restrict resources and operation surfaces —
the official recommendation is to connect MCP with a restricted token. This is the finest-grained credential line among its peers,
but "able to deploy code to Workers" means able to run arbitrary code — defend against that worst case.
axes.fit:
Fits: the agent deployment flow on the Cloudflare stack (write Worker → deploy → check logs), docs retrieval.
Not a fit: a hard "configure but never deploy" boundary (token granularity can narrow it, but must be configured carefully).

mcp.auth:
A Cloudflare API token (a restricted token is recommended: limit account/resources/operations);
OAuth-line support status not verified item by item.
mcp.scope:
Read surface: docs retrieval, resource queries; write surface: deploying Workers, creating/modifying D1/R2/KV, DNS record changes.
Token granularity is the primary tightening control; no official statement of a tool-level approval mechanism.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).

related: Also a model of the "multiple trimmable toolsets" design: GitHub uses toolsets; Cloudflare splits servers by product.
